answers.reasoning: y^2=4px gives p=5; focus (5,0), directrix x=-5, so a+b-c=5+0-(-5)=10.
Ellipse has semiaxes 5,3 and positive focus coordinate 4; full axis lengths m=10,n=6, hence m+n+p=20.
Transverse axis length 6 gives a=3; c=5 and c^2=a^2+b^2 give b=4; a+b=7.
Normalize to x^2/4-y^2/3=1; asymptote slope is sqrt(3)/2, equal to tan(theta).
Implicit differentiation gives 2x+3y+(3x-6y)y'=0; solve for y'.

Using unit-hexagon coordinates A=(-1/2,sqrt(3)/2), F=(1/2,sqrt(3)/2), E=(1,0), D=(1/2,-sqrt(3)/2), C=(-1/2,-sqrt(3)/2), B=(-1,0), the three displayed vector equalities/norm are true; the last sum is (2,-2sqrt(3)) with norm 4.
dy/dt=2e^(2t+3), dx/dt=e^(t+1); their ratio is 2e^(t+2).
Parallelism gives (a,2)=-(3,-2), so a=-3; perpendicularity gives (-3,2) dot (-4,b)=12+2b=0, b=-6.
With A as origin, M=(a+b)/2 and K=(a+b)/4; BK=K-a=(-3/4)a+(1/4)b, so m+n=-1/2.
For a regular hexagon centered at O, sum of vertex position vectors is zero; AB+AC+AD+AE+AF=-6OA, whose norm is 6 times the side length. Thus side=12/6=2.
P and Q are each affine combinations of A,B with coefficient sum 1 (internal and external division); their midpoint M also has coefficient sum 1, so s+t=1.
The two line direction vectors are (1,m) and (4,2). For m=2, cosine of the angle between them is |8+4|/(sqrt(5)sqrt(20))=4/5; among listed integer choices this gives m=2.
AP dot BP=0 describes the circle with diameter AB; center is (0,2) and r^2=|AB|^2/4=32/4=8, so a+b+r^2=10.
One tangent is vertical at x=2 (ellipse rightmost point); the other has slope 2 from the tangent condition. The acute angle to a vertical line has tan=1/2, so sin+cos=(1+2)/sqrt(5)=3sqrt(5)/5.
dy/dx=(t^n-1)/(t^2-1), whose limit at t=1 is n/2; multiplying by 8/n gives 4.
For d=a dot b, squaring the condition gives 6kd=k^2+1. Since k>0, d=(k+1/k)/6 is minimized at k=1, giving cos(theta)=d=1/3.
The two radius-2 disks have centers distance 2sqrt(2); their lens area is 2pi-4. The half-plane x+y<=2 selects exactly half the symmetric lens, so area=pi-2.
The vector equation makes P the centroid: P=((6,12)+(4,5)+(8,7))/3=(6,8), so OP=10.
At t=1, (x,y)=(5,5); dy/dx=(6t+2)/2=4, hence tangent y-5=4(x-5).
Subtract the given position vectors. Collinearity of coefficient pairs (-5,1) and (2,-k-1) requires determinant 5k+3=0.

At P=(3,1), the hyperbola tangent is x-y=2. Its intersections with y=x/sqrt(3) and y=-x/sqrt(3) have squared distances from O equal to 16+8sqrt(3) and 16-8sqrt(3); the product of distances is sqrt(64)=8.
From the opened grid, a=(-2,2), b=(-3,1), c=(3,5). Solving c=pa+qb gives 2p+q=5 and -2p-3q=3, hence p=9/2,q=-4 and p+q=1/2.
